newsitem.title: CHINA: China completes $2.4 bln railway in poor southwest.
newsitem.headline: China completes $2.4 bln railway in poor southwest.

text.p: China has finished laying track for an 899-km electrified railway in its mountainous southwest in a project that has cost nearly 20 billion yuan ($2.4 billion), the China Daily said on Wednesday.
The rail line links Kunming in Yunnan province, through neighbouring Guizhou province and Nanning in the Guangxi region, the newspaper said.
The central government had provided most of the funds needed to build the railway and had secured a Japanese loan worth about 4.6 billion yuan, it said.

The line had the largest unit cost of any railway in China because of mountainous terrain along the route, it quoted Zhou Zhenyuan, director of the construction department of the Ministry of Railways, as saying.
The new line, which was begun in 1990 and soars to 2,000 metres above sea level, was part of a plan by Beijing to boost economic development in poor and backwards areas, Zhou said.
An estimated 15 million people lived in poverty along the line, the newspaper said.
"Though expensive and difficult, the line had to be built," Zhou said. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
